definition: to gradually wear away or weaken something

examples.text: Wind and rain eroded the sandstone into arches.
Years of inflation eroded the value of soldiers' pay.
Missing three practices in a row eroded the coach's trust in me.

confused.note: To erode is to wear away gradually by wind, water, or time; to corrode is to eat away chemically.

questions.passage: Public confidence in the bank did not collapse overnight. It was ______ over several years, as one small scandal after another suggested that managers cared more for bonuses than for customers' savings.
questions.explanation: Confidence weakened gradually, scandal by scandal.

distractors.why: Reinforced means strengthened, the opposite of what the scandals did.
Deduced means concluded by reasoning, which does not fit.
Indulged means gave in to a desire, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin rodere, "to gnaw": to gnaw away

definition: to reach a conclusion by reasoning from the facts you have

examples.text: From the tilt of the rock layers, geologists deduced that the valley had once been a sea.
The detective deduces from a muddy boot that the visitor came by the river path.
I deduced from the crumbs that my brother had found the cookies.

confused.note: To deduce is to reason to a conclusion; to deduct is to subtract.

questions.passage: No one saw the thief enter. From the unbroken locks and the single open window on the third floor, however, the inspector ______ that the intruder had climbed the drainpipe.
questions.explanation: Reasoning from the locks and window to a conclusion is deducing.

distractors.why: Impaired means weakened, which does not fit.
Shunned means deliberately avoided, which does not fit.
Preceded means came before, which does not fit.

definition: to damage something or make it weaker or less effective

examples.text: Lack of sleep impairs memory and reaction time.
The loss of the fleet impaired the kingdom's ability to trade.
Loud music can impair your hearing for good.

confused.note: To impair is to weaken; to impart is to give or share.

questions.passage: Doctors warn that even small amounts of the drug can ______ a driver's judgment. In tests, volunteers who had taken a single dose braked a full second later than those who had not.
questions.explanation: Slower braking shows the drug weakens judgment.

distractors.why: Reinforce means to strengthen, the opposite of the drug's effect.
Deduce means to reason out, which does not fit.
Indulge means to give in to a wish, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin pejor, "worse": to make worse

definition: to come or happen before something else

examples.text: A drop in pressure often precedes a storm.
Years of unrest preceded the revolution.
A long silence preceded my dad's answer, which is never a good sign.

confused.note: To precede is to come before; to proceed is to go forward.

questions.passage: The earthquake did not strike without warning. It was ______ by a series of small tremors, which instruments recorded over the previous two weeks but which few residents noticed.
questions.explanation: Tremors that came before the earthquake preceded it.

distractors.why: Eroded means worn away, which does not fit.
Reinforced means strengthened, which does not fit.
Shunned means avoided, which does not fit.

definition: something said or done to show great respect for someone

examples.text: Each new knight paid homage to the queen on bended knee.
The novel is an homage to the detective stories its author loved as a child.
The band played their old teacher's favorite song as an homage.

confused.note: Homage is a show of respect; a hostage is a person held captive.

questions.passage: The film is the director's ______ to the silent comedies of the 1920s. It uses no dialogue, was shot in black and white, and borrows several of its jokes directly from the masters of that era.
questions.explanation: Imitating beloved older films out of respect is paying tribute.

distractors.why: Volition is the act of willing or choosing, which does not fit.
Sustenance is nourishment, which does not fit.
Prestige is high standing, which a film cannot be "to" something.

definition: completely lacking something

examples.text: The moon is devoid of atmosphere.
Her voice was devoid of any warmth.
The fridge was devoid of anything I wanted to eat.

confused.note: Devoid means completely lacking; to avoid is to keep away from.

questions.passage: The report is entirely ______ of evidence. In forty pages its authors make dozens of confident claims and do not once cite a study, a statistic, or a named source.
questions.explanation: A report that cites nothing completely lacks evidence.

distractors.why: Innumerable means too many to count, and it does not fit "of evidence."
Imposing means grand and impressive, which does not fit.
Tepid means lukewarm, which does not fit.

definition: famous and greatly admired for past achievements

examples.text: The academy counted three illustrious generals among its graduates.
The hero is the last, and least impressive, of an illustrious family.
Our school's most illustrious graduate is a retired weather forecaster.

confused.note: Illustrious means famous and admired; illustrative means serving as an example.

questions.passage: The orchestra has an ______ history. Founded in 1842, it has given the first performances of more than sixty major works and has been led by nearly every great conductor of the past century.
questions.explanation: Famous premieres and great conductors make a history worthy of admiration.

distractors.why: Minuscule means tiny, which does not fit.
Tepid means lukewarm, which does not fit.
Curt means rudely brief, which does not fit.

definition: good at thinking of new and original ideas

examples.text: An inventive graduate student built the detector from spare bicycle parts.
The novel's inventive structure tells its story backward.
My sister is inventive with leftovers and once made soup from a taco.

confused.note: Inventive means creative; an inventory is a list of goods.

questions.passage: With no budget for scenery, the school's drama teacher had to be ______. She built a forest from umbrellas, a river from blue bedsheets, and a castle from cardboard boxes painted gray.
questions.explanation: Making scenery from umbrellas and boxes shows original, creative thinking.

distractors.why: Autocratic means domineering, which is not what the examples show.
Hostile means unfriendly, which does not fit.
Stark means bare or harsh, which does not describe her cleverness.

definition: to deliberately avoid someone or something

examples.text: After the scandal, the court shunned the disgraced minister.
The village shuns the widow who refuses to wear black.
I shun the cafeteria on fish stick day.

confused.note: To shun is to avoid on purpose; to stun is to shock.

questions.passage: The author has always ______ publicity. She gives no interviews, has never appeared at a book signing, and is known to her millions of readers only through a single photograph taken forty years ago.
questions.explanation: Giving no interviews and making no appearances is deliberately avoiding publicity.

distractors.why: Indulged means gave in to or enjoyed freely, the opposite of avoiding.
Reinforced means strengthened, which does not fit.
Deduced means reasoned out, which does not fit.

definition: too many to be counted

examples.text: The night sky away from the city shows innumerable stars.
The archive holds innumerable letters that no historian has yet read.
I have told my brother innumerable times not to borrow my charger.

confused.note: Innumerable means too many to count; "enumerable" means able to be counted.

questions.passage: The explorer's journals describe ______ hardships. Scarcely a page passes without mention of a lost mule, a spoiled sack of flour, a flooded camp, or a guide who vanished in the night.
questions.explanation: Hardships on nearly every page are too many to count.

distractors.why: Minuscule means tiny, which does not describe a great number.
Devoid means completely lacking, which does not fit.
Tepid means lukewarm, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin numerus, "number": not able to be numbered

definition: extremely small

examples.text: The chip contains minuscule wires a thousand times thinner than a hair.
The duchy was minuscule, smaller than many farms.
My share of the pizza was minuscule after my brothers got to it.

confused.note: The standard spelling is "minuscule," related to "minus."

questions.passage: The risk of the treatment is ______. Of the two million patients who have received it, only three have suffered serious side effects, and all three recovered fully.
questions.explanation: Three cases in two million is an extremely small risk.

distractors.why: Innumerable means too many to count, the opposite of three cases.
Imposing means grand, which does not fit.
Illustrious means famous and admired, which does not fit.

definition: food and drink that keeps people, animals, or plants alive; support

examples.text: The fungus draws its sustenance from the roots of the tree.
The besieged town had sustenance for only three more weeks.
A granola bar was my only sustenance on the four-hour bus ride.

confused.note: Sustenance is nourishment; substance is matter or importance.

questions.passage: During the long polar night, the expedition's dogs provided more than transport. In the final desperate weeks they were also the men's only source of ______.
questions.explanation: Being the only source of food is providing what keeps people alive.

distractors.why: Homage is a show of respect, which does not fit.
Volition is will or choice, which does not fit.
Prestige is high standing, which does not fit.

definition: ruling with complete power; demanding total obedience

examples.text: The autocratic governor dissolved the council and ruled by decree.
The autocratic headmaster allows no question he has not already answered.
My brother becomes autocratic whenever he is put in charge of the remote.

confused.note: Autocratic means ruling with total power; aristocratic means belonging to the nobility.

questions.passage: The company's founder ran it in an ______ fashion. She made every decision herself, tolerated no disagreement in meetings, and dismissed three executives who suggested that she delegate.
questions.explanation: Deciding everything alone and punishing dissent is ruling with total control.

distractors.why: Inventive means creative, which is not what the examples show.
Tepid means lukewarm, which does not fit.
Relevant means connected to the matter, which does not fit.

definition: the power to choose or decide for yourself

examples.text: The king insisted that he had abdicated of his own volition.
A reflex happens without volition; you cannot choose not to blink.
No one made me join the choir; I signed up of my own volition.

confused.note: Volition is free will; a violation is the breaking of a rule.

questions.passage: The minister denied that she had been forced out. She had left the government, she said, entirely of her own ______, having decided months earlier that she wished to return to teaching.
questions.explanation: Leaving by her own decision is acting of her own free will.

distractors.why: Sustenance is nourishment, which does not fit.
Homage is a show of respect, which does not fit.
Dominion is power or rule over others, which does not fit "of her own."

definition: slightly warm; or showing little enthusiasm

examples.text: The eggs hatch only in tepid water, neither cold nor hot.
The play received tepid applause and closed within a week.
The soup was tepid by the time I finished taking photos of it.

confused.note: Tepid means lukewarm or unenthusiastic; torpid means sluggish and inactive.

questions.passage: The audience's response to the long speech was ______ at best. A few people clapped politely when it ended, but most were already reaching for their coats.
questions.explanation: Polite clapping from a few shows little enthusiasm.

distractors.why: Hostile means openly unfriendly, too strong for mild indifference.
Illustrious means famous and admired, which does not fit.
Stark means harsh or bare, which does not fit.

definition: large and impressive in appearance

examples.text: Ambassadors waited in the imposing hall beneath a ceiling forty meters high.
The headmistress is an imposing figure in black silk.
The new library is an imposing building for such a small town.

confused.note: Imposing means impressive; an imposition is an unfair demand.

questions.passage: Travelers approaching the city first see its ______ cathedral. Its twin towers rise ninety meters above the plain and can be seen from villages a day's walk away.
questions.explanation: Towers visible from a day's walk away are large and impressive.

distractors.why: Minuscule means tiny, the opposite of a towering cathedral.
Curt means rudely brief, which does not fit.
Counterproductive means working against one's goal, which does not fit.

definition: unfriendly and ready to fight or argue; opposed

examples.text: The explorers crossed hostile territory by night.
Few plants survive in the hostile conditions of the salt flats.
The crowd turned hostile when the referee disallowed the goal.

confused.note: Hostile means unfriendly; a hostel is cheap lodging for travelers.

questions.passage: The proposal met a ______ reception. Residents booed the mayor when she rose to speak, and several shouted that they would block the bulldozers with their own bodies.
questions.explanation: Booing and threats to block bulldozers show angry opposition.

distractors.why: Tepid means lukewarm, far too mild for booing and threats.
Imposing means impressive, which does not fit.
Inventive means creative, which does not fit.

definition: very plain and without decoration; or unpleasantly clear and impossible to avoid

examples.text: The data show a stark difference between the two groups.
The stark landscape of rock and ice offers nowhere to hide.
The stark white walls of the new apartment needed posters.

confused.note: Stark means bare or harsh; a stork is a long-legged bird.

questions.passage: The photographs present a ______ contrast. On one side of the fence, where grazing was forbidden, the grass grows waist high; on the other, the ground is bare dust.
questions.explanation: Tall grass beside bare dust is a sharp, unmistakable contrast.

distractors.why: Marginal means slight, the opposite of so sharp a difference.
Tepid means lukewarm, which does not describe a contrast.
Curt means rudely brief, which does not fit.

definition: the respect and admiration that someone or something has because of success or high quality

examples.text: Victory at sea brought the small republic enormous prestige.
Publication in that journal carries great prestige.
Being chosen as captain carries a certain prestige and a lot of extra work.

confused.note: Prestige is the noun; prestigious is the adjective.

questions.passage: The university's ______ rests largely on its medical school. Graduates of the program lead hospitals on five continents, and admission to it is sought by ten thousand applicants a year.
questions.explanation: Sought-after admission and distinguished graduates bring respect and admiration.

distractors.why: Volition is free will, which does not fit.
Sustenance is nourishment, which does not fit.
Sentiment is feeling or opinion, which does not fit.

definition: to make something stronger

examples.text: Steel rods reinforce the concrete against earthquakes.
The king reinforced the border forts before winter.
Praise reinforces good habits better than nagging does.

confused.note: To reinforce is to strengthen; to enforce is to make people obey a rule.

questions.passage: Engineers feared that the old dam could not withstand another flood. They ______ it with a second wall of concrete, anchored by steel cables driven thirty meters into the rock.
questions.explanation: Adding a second wall and cables made the dam stronger.

distractors.why: Eroded means wore away, the opposite of strengthening.
Impaired means weakened, which is not what the engineers did.
Preceded means came before, which does not fit.

definition: to allow yourself or someone else to enjoy something, especially something not really needed

examples.text: The young king indulged his taste for hunting while his ministers ruled.
Grandmother indulges the children with sweets their mother has forbidden.
I indulged in a second slice of cake after the exam.

confused.note: Indulge is the verb; indulgent is the adjective meaning lenient.

questions.passage: The retired general lived simply but ______ one expensive taste. Each spring he ordered rare tulip bulbs from abroad, and his garden became the wonder of the county.
questions.explanation: Allowing himself one costly pleasure is indulging it.

distractors.why: Shunned means avoided, the opposite of allowing himself the pleasure.
Impaired means weakened, which does not fit.
Eroded means wore away, which does not fit.

definition: rudely brief in speech or manner

examples.text: The butler's curt "Not at home" ends the visit before it begins.
The general sent a curt refusal to the offer of talks.
Her curt "fine" told me that things were not fine.

confused.note: Curt means rudely brief; a court is a place of law or a royal household.

questions.passage: Reporters waiting outside the ministry had hoped for a full statement. They received only a ______ reply: "No comment," said the minister, and closed the car door.
questions.explanation: A two-word answer and a closed door are rudely brief.

distractors.why: Imposing means grand and impressive, which does not fit.
Illustrious means famous and admired, which does not fit.
Innumerable means countless, which does not fit.

definition: having the opposite effect to the one intended

examples.text: Overwatering is counterproductive; it rots the roots it is meant to feed.
The harsh new taxes proved counterproductive and reduced the crown's income.
Studying all night before the test was counterproductive.

confused.note: Counterproductive means working against one's own goal; a counterpart is a matching person or thing.

questions.passage: The ban on street vendors was meant to reduce litter. It proved ______: with no stalls nearby, office workers bought lunch in packaging from distant shops, and the amount of rubbish in the square doubled.
questions.explanation: A measure that doubled the litter it was meant to reduce had the opposite effect.

distractors.why: Relevant means connected to the matter, which does not fit.
Inventive means creative, which does not describe a failed ban.
Autocratic means domineering, which is not the point.

definition: directly connected with the subject or problem being discussed

examples.text: Only studies relevant to the question were included in the review.
The judge admitted only the letters relevant to the case.
Your story is funny but not relevant to who left the gate open.

confused.note: Relevant means connected to the matter; reverent means showing deep respect.

questions.passage: The judge instructed the jury to consider only ______ evidence. What the defendant had done ten years earlier in another country, she said, had no bearing on the question before them.
questions.explanation: Evidence with a bearing on the question is connected to it.

distractors.why: Stark means bare or harsh, which does not fit.
Tepid means lukewarm, which does not fit.
Devoid means completely lacking, which does not fit.

definition: to improve a system, law, or organization by making changes to it

examples.text: The new queen reformed the courts and abolished trial by combat.
The society voted to reform the way it reviews papers.
The student council promised to reform the lunch line.

confused.note: To reform is to change for the better; to conform is to follow the rules.

questions.passage: The new minister set out to ______ the prison system. She closed the three oldest jails, ended the practice of holding children with adults, and required that every inmate be taught to read.
questions.explanation: Changing the system to improve it is reforming it.

distractors.why: Erode means to wear away, which does not describe deliberate improvement.
Precede means to come before, which does not fit.
Shun means to avoid, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin formare, "to shape": to shape again

definition: relating to the treatment of patients; or cool, detached, and unemotional

examples.text: The drug is now in clinical trials with two thousand volunteers.
The narrator describes his own heartbreak in oddly clinical language.
The new kitchen is so white and clinical that I am afraid to cook in it.

confused.note: Clinical means medical or coolly detached; cynical means distrustful of motives.

questions.passage: The report describes the disaster in ______ terms. It lists the number of dead, the cost of repairs, and the sequence of mechanical failures, and it does not once mention how the survivors felt.
questions.explanation: Listing facts with no mention of feeling is cool and detached.

distractors.why: Ambitious means eager to succeed, which does not fit.
Peculiar means strange, which is not what the details show.
Tremendous means very great, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Greek kline, "bed": at the bedside

definition: a way of approaching a problem or making progress; a wide street

examples.text: Gene therapy offers a promising avenue for treating the disease.
With the port closed, the only avenue of trade was over the mountains.
I have explored every avenue for getting concert tickets, including begging my cousin.

confused.note: An avenue is a route or approach; a venue is the place where an event is held.

questions.passage: Having failed to persuade the council, the residents turned to another ______. They collected four thousand signatures and forced the question onto the ballot at the next election.
questions.explanation: A different way of pursuing their goal is another approach.

distractors.why: A decree is an official order, which residents cannot issue.
Dominion is rule or control, which does not fit.
Sentiment is feeling or opinion, which does not fit "turned to another."

definition: to increase or improve something

examples.text: Vitamin C does not prevent colds, but it may boost recovery slightly.
The new canal boosted trade between the two cities.
A good breakfast boosts my mood until at least second period.

confused.note: To boost is to raise or improve; to boast is to brag.

questions.passage: The town hoped that the festival would ______ tourism. In its first year the event drew thirty thousand visitors, and hotel bookings for the month tripled.
questions.explanation: Tripled bookings show tourism increased.

distractors.why: Adapt means to adjust to new conditions, which does not fit.
Behold means to look at, which does not fit.
Demonstrate means to show, which is not what the town hoped to do to tourism.

definition: a basic truth, rule, or belief that guides behavior or explains how something works

examples.text: The engine works on the principle that hot gas expands.
The charter rested on the principle that no one is above the law.
As a matter of principle, I never read the last page of a book first.

confused.note: A principle is a rule or belief; a principal is the head of a school, or as an adjective, main.

questions.passage: The scientist refused the company's money on ______. She believed that research paid for by those who profit from its results cannot be trusted, and she would not make an exception even for her own laboratory.
questions.explanation: Refusing because of a belief about how research should be funded is acting on a guiding rule.

distractors.why: Sentiment is feeling; her refusal rests on a reasoned belief.
Prestige is high standing, which does not fit.
An ideology is a whole system of political ideas, broader than a single rule of conduct.

definition: causing a lot of disagreement because many people have strong opinions about it

examples.text: The treaty was controversial from the day it was signed.
The theory remained controversial until new fossils were found.
Pineapple on pizza is a controversial topic in my house.

confused.note: Controversial means causing disagreement; contradictory means saying opposite things.

questions.passage: The decision to move the statue proved highly ______. Letters for and against filled the newspaper for a month, and two members of the council resigned in protest.
questions.explanation: Letters on both sides and resignations show strong disagreement.

distractors.why: Marginal means slight or minor, the opposite of a heated dispute.
Quantitative means relating to numbers, which does not fit.
Modest means humble or small, which does not fit.

definition: to show clearly that something is true; to show how something works

examples.text: The experiment demonstrates that sound cannot travel through a vacuum.
The march demonstrated how widely the tax was hated.
My brother demonstrated how to flip a pancake and dropped it on the dog.

confused.note: To demonstrate is to show; to remonstrate is to protest or complain.

questions.passage: Critics doubted that a bridge so light could carry heavy traffic. To ______ its strength, the engineers drove forty loaded trucks onto the span at once and left them there for a day.
questions.explanation: Loading the bridge with trucks shows clearly that it is strong.

distractors.why: Decree means to order officially, which does not fit.
Adapt means to adjust, which does not fit.
Behold means to look at, which does not fit.

definition: very great in amount, size, or degree

examples.text: The collision released a tremendous amount of energy.
The canal required a tremendous effort from sixty thousand workers.
I felt a tremendous sense of relief when the test was over.

confused.note: Tremendous means very great; tremulous means shaking or timid.

questions.passage: The eruption released ______ energy. The blast was heard three thousand kilometers away, and ash from the volcano circled the globe, coloring sunsets for more than a year.
questions.explanation: A blast heard thousands of kilometers away involves a very great amount of energy.

distractors.why: Marginal means slight, the opposite of so great a release.
Null means having no value or effect, which does not fit.
Clinical means medical or detached, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin tremere, "to tremble": causing trembling

definition: not large in size or amount; or not boastful about your own abilities

examples.text: The drug produced a modest improvement, nothing dramatic.
The great general lived in a modest house of four rooms.
She is modest about her grades, though she has the best in the class.

confused.note: Modest means humble or not large; modish means fashionable.

questions.passage: The company's profits rose last year, but the increase was ______. At two percent, it barely kept pace with rising costs and fell well short of what investors had hoped.
questions.explanation: A two percent rise that disappointed investors is not large.

distractors.why: Tremendous means very great, the opposite of a two percent rise.
Abundant means plentiful, which does not describe a small increase.
Controversial means causing dispute, which does not fit.

definition: a feeling or opinion, especially one based on emotion

examples.text: Public sentiment turned against the war after the second winter.
The poem expresses a sentiment every homesick traveler will know.
I appreciate the sentiment, but I really do not need a third scarf.

confused.note: A sentiment is a feeling or opinion; sediment is matter that settles at the bottom of a liquid.

questions.passage: The mayor misjudged public ______. She had assumed that residents would welcome the new stadium, but a survey showed that seven in ten would have preferred a park.
questions.explanation: What residents feel and prefer is public opinion.

distractors.why: Dominion is rule or control, which does not fit.
An avenue is a route or approach, which does not fit.
A decree is an official order, which does not fit.

definition: a set of beliefs or ideas on which a political or economic system is based

examples.text: The two parties shared an enemy but not an ideology.
The author warns against letting ideology decide which results get published.
My uncle turns every dinner into a debate about ideology.

confused.note: An ideology is a system of beliefs; an idiom is a phrase whose meaning differs from its words.

questions.passage: The two revolutionary leaders agreed that the king must go. They differed sharply in ______, however: one wished to divide the land among the peasants, while the other hoped to hand it to a new class of merchants.
questions.explanation: Different visions of how society should be organized are different systems of belief.

distractors.why: An onset is a beginning, which does not fit.
An apex is a highest point, which does not fit.
An avenue is a route, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Greek idea, "form, idea": the study of ideas

definition: to change something or yourself to suit new conditions

examples.text: The finches adapted to the drought by eating harder seeds.
The army adapted its tactics to the mountain terrain.
I adapted my grandmother's recipe by using what was in the fridge.

confused.note: To adapt is to change to fit; to adopt is to take as one's own. Adept means skilled.

questions.passage: Camels are remarkably well ______ to desert life. They can go two weeks without water, their wide feet do not sink in sand, and a double row of eyelashes keeps out blowing grit.
questions.explanation: Features that suit the desert show the camel has changed to fit its conditions.

distractors.why: Decreed means officially ordered, which does not fit.
Spurred means urged on, which does not fit "to desert life."
Boosted means increased, which does not fit.

definition: having a strong desire to succeed; requiring great effort or skill

examples.text: The ambitious young officer was a general by thirty.
The plan to map every star in the galaxy is ambitious.
Making a three-tier cake for my first attempt was ambitious.

confused.note: Ambitious means eager to succeed; ambiguous means unclear.

questions.passage: The architect's plan was ______. She proposed not merely a new library but an entire district, with a concert hall, three museums, and a park built on a platform over the railway.
questions.explanation: A plan for a whole district demands great effort and aims high.

distractors.why: Modest means small in scale, the opposite of this plan.
Marginal means minor, which this plan was not.
Clinical means detached, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin ambire, "to go around" seeking votes

definition: quickly and easily; willingly

examples.text: Salt dissolves readily in warm water.
The merchants readily agreed to a tax that protected their ships.
My dog readily forgives me for stepping on his tail.

confused.note: Readily means easily or willingly; really means truly.

questions.passage: The witness did not have to be pressed. She ______ admitted that she had been in the building that night and offered, without being asked, to describe everyone she had seen.
questions.explanation: Admitting without pressure and volunteering more is doing so willingly.

distractors.why: Marginally means slightly, which does not describe how she admitted it.
Modestly means humbly; the point is that she needed no urging.
Abundantly means plentifully, which does not fit.

definition: an official order made by a ruler or government

examples.text: By royal decree, every village had to maintain a stretch of road.
The mayor's decree that hats be removed in the square is the story's first joke.
By parental decree, phones stay downstairs after nine.

confused.note: A decree is an official order; a degree is a unit of measure or an academic title.

questions.passage: The king did not trouble to consult the assembly. He simply issued a ______ declaring that all foreign merchants must leave the port within thirty days.
questions.explanation: An order issued by a king on his own authority is a decree.

distractors.why: A sentiment is a feeling or opinion, not an order.
An avenue is a route or approach, which does not fit.
An advent is an arrival, which does not fit.

definition: existing in large quantities; more than enough

examples.text: Fossils of the shellfish are abundant in the cliffs along the coast.
The valley's abundant water made it the first to be settled.
Zucchini is so abundant in August that neighbors leave it on doorsteps.

confused.note: Abundant means plentiful; redundant means unnecessary because repeated.

questions.passage: Fish were once so ______ in the bay that early visitors claimed they could be caught by lowering a basket over the side of a boat. Today a full day's fishing may yield only a handful.
questions.explanation: Fish that could be caught with a basket existed in large quantities.

distractors.why: Marginal means slight, the opposite of such plenty.
Null means of no value or effect, which does not fit.
Peculiar means strange, which does not fit.

definition: to look at or see something, especially something impressive

examples.text: The travelers reach the ridge and behold the sea for the first time.
Crowds gathered to behold the first balloon rise over the city.
Behold my science fair volcano, which actually erupted.

confused.note: To behold is to look at; beholden means owing a debt of gratitude.

questions.passage: After nine days of climbing through cloud, the expedition broke into sunlight. Its members stood in silence to ______ the peaks of the range spread out below them, pink in the early light.
questions.explanation: Standing in silence to look at an impressive sight is beholding it.

distractors.why: Spur means to urge on, which does not fit.
Adapt means to adjust, which does not fit.
Boost means to raise, which does not fit.

definition: having no legal force; having no value or effect

examples.text: The court declared the forced treaty null and void.
The study reported a null result: the drug did nothing.
Our bet was null once we learned the game had been cancelled.

confused.note: Null means without force or value; dull means boring or not sharp.

questions.passage: Because one of the two parties had signed under threat, the judge ruled the contract ______. Neither side, she said, was bound by any of its terms.
questions.explanation: A contract with no binding terms has no legal force.

distractors.why: Abundant means plentiful, which does not fit.
Peculiar means strange; the ruling concerns legal force.
Marginal means minor; the contract has no force at all, not a small one.

definition: relating to amounts that can be measured or counted

examples.text: The study combines quantitative data with interviews.
Tax rolls give historians a quantitative picture of village life.
I want a quantitative answer: exactly how many cookies did you eat?

confused.note: Quantitative concerns how much or how many; qualitative concerns what kind.

questions.passage: The first part of the report is ______. It gives the number of patients treated, the average length of their stay, and the percentage who returned within a year; opinions about the quality of care come later.
questions.explanation: Numbers, averages, and percentages are measurable amounts.

distractors.why: Controversial means causing dispute, which does not fit.
Peculiar means strange, which does not fit.
Ambitious means aiming high, which is not what the list of figures shows.

definition: the beginning of something, especially something unpleasant

examples.text: The onset of symptoms usually comes two days after infection.
The army hurried to cross the pass before the onset of winter.
I can feel the onset of a cold: scratchy throat, heavy head.

confused.note: An onset is a beginning; to offset is to balance out.

questions.passage: Farmers in the region watch the sky closely in late spring. The ______ of the rains determines when they plant, and a delay of even two weeks can cut the harvest in half.
questions.explanation: The time the rains begin is their onset.

distractors.why: An apex is a highest point, not a beginning.
Dominion is rule or control, which does not fit.
A decree is an official order, which does not fit.

definition: the highest point of something; the peak

examples.text: The lion sits at the apex of the food chain.
The empire reached its apex under her rule.
The apex of my baking career was a cake that did not collapse.

confused.note: The apex is the top; apiece means each.

questions.passage: The singer's career reached its ______ in 1975, when she sold out forty stadiums in a single summer. Within five years, changing tastes had reduced her to playing small clubs.
questions.explanation: Selling out stadiums before a decline marks the highest point.

distractors.why: An onset is a beginning, but this was the peak before her decline.
An advent is an arrival, which does not fit.
An avenue is a route, which does not fit.

definition: small and not important; at the edge

examples.text: The new fertilizer produced only a marginal increase in yield.
The island played a marginal role in the war.
The difference in price was marginal, so I bought the nicer one.

confused.note: Marginal means slight or at the edge; marital relates to marriage.

questions.passage: The new engine uses less fuel, but the improvement is ______. In tests it traveled only one kilometer farther on a full tank than the engine it replaced.
questions.explanation: One extra kilometer per tank is a small, unimportant gain.

distractors.why: Tremendous means very great, the opposite of one kilometer.
Abundant means plentiful, which does not fit.
Controversial means causing dispute, which does not fit.

definition: the arrival of an important person, event, or invention

examples.text: The advent of the microscope revealed a world no one had imagined.
The advent of the railway ended the age of the stagecoach.
The advent of streaming ended our family's Friday trips to the video store.

confused.note: An advent is an arrival; an adventure is an exciting experience.

questions.passage: Before the ______ of refrigeration, people preserved food by salting, drying, or smoking it. Fresh meat could be had only where animals were slaughtered, and ice was a luxury carried down from the mountains.
questions.explanation: The arrival of a new technology is its advent.

distractors.why: An apex is a highest point, not an arrival.
A decree is an official order, which does not fit.
A sentiment is a feeling, which does not fit.

definition: strange or unusual; or belonging only to one person, place, or thing

examples.text: The species has a peculiar habit of sleeping upside down.
A peculiar silence falls over the house at noon.
The milk had a peculiar smell, so I poured it out.

confused.note: Peculiar means strange or unique to something; particular means specific or fussy.

questions.passage: The clock has a ______ feature that has puzzled collectors for years. Its hands run backward, and its face is numbered from twelve down to one.
questions.explanation: A clock that runs backward is strange and unusual.

distractors.why: Marginal means minor, which does not capture strangeness.
Quantitative means numerical, which does not fit.
Abundant means plentiful, which does not fit.

definition: power or the right to rule over people or land; a territory that is ruled

examples.text: The king claimed dominion over every island within sight of his coast.
The dragon holds dominion over the valley and all who cross it.
My older sister claims dominion over the entire top bunk.

confused.note: Dominion is the power to rule; a domain is the area ruled or a field of knowledge.

questions.passage: At its height the empire held ______ over a quarter of the world's population. Its governors collected taxes on five continents, and its laws were enforced in more than a hundred languages.
questions.explanation: Collecting taxes and enforcing laws across continents is ruling over them.

distractors.why: Sentiment is feeling or opinion, which does not fit.
An advent is an arrival, which does not fit.
An onset is a beginning, which does not fit.

definition: to encourage someone to act or to make something happen faster

examples.text: The discovery of gold spurred a rush of settlers to the west.
The outbreak spurred research into a new vaccine.
A bad grade on the first quiz spurred me to start studying.

confused.note: To spur is to urge on; to spurn is to reject with contempt.

questions.passage: The prize was created to ______ innovation. Any team that could build a car capable of traveling a hundred kilometers on a single liter of fuel would receive ten million dollars.
questions.explanation: A large prize encourages teams to invent.

distractors.why: Spurn means to reject with contempt; it resembles the right word but means nearly the opposite.
Behold means to look at, which does not fit.
Decree means to order officially; a prize encourages, it does not command.
